blocks.text: Ever wondered why your trial balance doesn't agree? Let's explore how errors and suspense accounts can help solve this mystery.

blocks.markdown: In accounting, errors can occur during the recording of transactions. These errors can affect the trial balance, leading to discrepancies. Understanding the types of errors and how to correct them is crucial for maintaining accurate financial records.

blocks.title: Types of Errors
blocks.text: Errors in accounting can be classified into errors of principle, errors of omission, errors of commission, and compensating errors.

blocks.markdown: Errors of principle occur when a transaction is recorded in violation of accounting principles. Errors of omission happen when a transaction is completely left out. Errors of commission occur when an entry is made in the wrong account. Compensating errors are multiple errors that cancel each other out.

blocks.title: Correcting Errors Using Journal Entries
blocks.prompt: A transaction of ₦5,000 for office supplies was mistakenly recorded as a purchase of equipment. Correct this error using a journal entry.

steps.text: Identify the error: The transaction was recorded in the Equipment account instead of the Office Supplies account.
Reverse the incorrect entry: Debit the Equipment account and credit the Office Supplies account for ₦5,000.
Record the correct entry: Debit the Office Supplies account and credit the Bank account for ₦5,000.

blocks.answer: Correct journal entry: Debit Office Supplies ₦5,000, Credit Equipment ₦5,000.

blocks.markdown: Sometimes, errors cause the trial balance to not agree. A suspense account is used temporarily to hold the difference until the errors are identified and corrected.

blocks.title: Using Suspense Accounts
blocks.text: When the trial balance doesn't agree, create a suspense account with the difference. Once errors are corrected, the suspense account should balance to zero.

points: Errors can be classified into different types, some affecting the trial balance and others not.
Suspense accounts are used to temporarily hold discrepancies in the trial balance.
